hints: Set the derivative equal to $0$ and solve for $\sqrt{x}$.
walkthrough:
Set $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ to locate the stationary maximum:
$$\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}} - 1 = 0 \implies \sqrt{x} = 2$$

Find the positive $x$-intercept $b$ by setting $y = 0$:
$$4\sqrt{x} - x = 0 \implies \sqrt{x}(4 - \sqrt{x}) = 0 \implies \sqrt{x} = 4 \implies b = 16$$

Set up the definite integral for the area from $x = 4$ to $x = 16$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_4^{16} (4x^{1/2} - x)\,dx = \left[\frac{8}{3}x^{3/2} - \frac{1}{2}x^2\right]_4^{16}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 4$ and subtract:
$$\frac{8}{3}(4^{3/2}) - \frac{1}{2}(4^2) = \frac{8}{3}(8) - 8 = \frac{64}{3} - 8 = \frac{40}{3}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{128}{3} - \frac{40}{3} = \frac{88}{3} = 29\frac{1}{3}$$
